item.text:
Yes—there’s a **browser-use QA** skill available here. It’s meant for inspecting and evaluating a running website; for setting up repeatable E2E automation in a Next.js repo, **Playwright** is a good default. Next.js has an official Playwright setup guide, and Playwright can start your app automatically before tests run. ([Next.js testing guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/testing), [Playwright web server config](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-webserver))

A basic setup is:

1. From your app directory, run `npm init playwright@latest` (or the equivalent for your package manager). Choose TypeScript and install the browsers you want to test.
2. Configure Playwright to start the app with `npm run dev`, wait for `http://localhost:3000`, and set that as `baseURL`.
3. Add tests for important user journeys—such as signing in, creating a record, or completing checkout—using accessible labels and roles to find elements.
4. Run `npx playwright test` locally; add it to your CI workflow so it runs on pull requests. ([Playwright installation](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro), [running tests](https://playwright.dev/docs/running-tests))

I couldn’t see your app files in the current workspace, so I can’t tailor the config to its package manager or scripts yet. If you open the app’s repo here, I can set up the Playwright files and a starter test for one of its real user flows.
